list: The official 55 trophies, as listed on Exophase and PSNProfiles before this guide was written (names, descriptions and grades agree on both).
sources_note: Every trophy's name, description and grade come from the official list on Exophase (exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies) and PSNProfiles (psnprofiles.com/trophies/43531-grand-theft-auto-vi). Each guide below is my own advice, drawn from that official description; where the description does not pin down a place or a step, the guide says so plainly instead of inventing one.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum: it pops on its own the moment you earn the other 54 trophies. There is nothing to chase directly, so work the roadmap in order — story first, missables as they come, then the long grinds — and treat this as the finish line. The last trophy you earn is usually 100% Completion or one of the big counters, so leave a grind you enjoy for last.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing. It is the first story mission of the game, so this pops naturally as you play through the opening — no preparation and no detour needed. If you are hunting efficiently, do not linger: the rest of the story unlocks after it.

While you are in Chapter 1, keep an eye out for the missable moments flagged in this guide — the chapter trophies themselves cannot be missed.

If the game offers a choice before the finale, save first: the 'Choices made' trophy suggests at least one decision matters.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own checklist. This is the second gold trophy and usually the last one earned before the platinum. 100% in GTA games means finishing the story, the side missions, the collectibles and the activities the checklist counts — open the in-game stats or checklist screen to see exactly what is still missing, and work through it category by category. Do not leave this to the very end blind: check your percentage regularly so a single forgotten activity does not surprise you.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near-misses, drifts, airtime and the like, as the game counts them. This is a slow counter that builds up across the whole playthrough, so do not grind it in one sitting: stunt naturally while travelling, and use ramps and jumps you pass. If you are short at the end, pick a fast vehicle and a route with jumps and repeat it. The in-game stats screen should show your stunt count; check it there rather than guessing.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types in the game once. PSN's target is 9 types, so the game counts nine distinct activities — the shooting range, drone races, races, fishing, arcade games and the other activities named across this list are the obvious candidates. The cheapest way is to sample one of each as you meet it instead of saving them all for the end: every time a new activity appears on the map, try it once and tick it off here.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is a silver trophy and one of the biggest skill grinds on the list, so treat it as a project: visit the range early to learn the scoring, then work through the challenges weapon by weapon. Gold usually means fast, accurate shooting with few misses — take your time on each challenge rather than rushing, and replay a challenge until the gold pops. The range is repeatable, so nothing here can be missed.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Drone races are repeatable, so learn the course on a first run and then race to win — cutting corners cleanly and keeping the drone level through gates matters more than raw speed. Work through the locations one at a time and tick them off here, so you know which 14 are done and which are still open. The official description does not name the locations; they appear on the map as you discover them.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word 'different' matters: winning the same race 20 times does not count — you need 20 distinct races won. Work through the race list across the map, one new race at a time, and keep a note of which you have won. Pick a fast, stable vehicle for each race type, learn the route on the first lap, and push on the second. Races are repeatable, so a loss costs nothing but time.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level and then lose it and escape. Flagged missable because it needs your partner present — a situation that only happens in certain missions and moments, not whenever you like. When you are out with your partner and the heat is on, do not just fight: break line of sight, get out of the search area, and stay hidden until the stars clear. Save before you try it, and do it the first time the chance appears rather than assuming it will come back.

Save first and attempt it the first time the setup is available.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Find something strange — the description reads like a reaction to an unexpected event, the kind of hidden oddity GTA games tuck away. Flagged missable because a one-off strange encounter may only trigger once, in one place. Explore odd corners of the map, investigate anything out of place, and save before interacting with something weird. This guide does not invent the location: the official description does not name one, so keep your eyes open while exploring Leonida.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock people over with a melee drive-by — attack from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon and bowl them over. Flagged missable because it needs a specific setup: a vehicle, a melee weapon, and a group of people in reach. Save first, drive slowly past a group on foot, swing as you pass, and keep going until the trophy pops. If the group scatters, find another one rather than chasing the same people on foot.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists and cannot be spent as-is, so take them to your contacts to wash them into clean cash. Keep laundering after every big score instead of letting Marked Bills pile up, and the $250,000 total climbs steadily. The counter is cumulative, so nothing here can be missed.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Every purchase counts — clothes, weapons, food, car mods, anything bought in a shop — so this climbs naturally as you gear up through the game. Do not save all your spending for the end: buy what you need as you go, and if you are short late on, spend the surplus on expensive items you will actually use, like weapon upgrades. The counter is cumulative across every shop.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy every garage property in the game. Garages are properties you purchase to store vehicles, and they appear on the map and through the property system as the story opens up. Buy each one as soon as you can afford it — garages are useful all game, not just for the trophy. The official description does not say how many garages there are; the in-game property list shows which ones you own and which are still for sale.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app is the in-game way to call and store vehicles — open it, register a vehicle you own or have found, and repeat until you reach 10. Use a mix of cars and bikes you actually drive so the registrations are useful, not just ten throwaway cars. The official description does not name the registration steps; the app's own screens walk you through them.
